podcast.title: Empowering Sex Worker Narrative
podcast.body: Released in 1974, this song about a hooker was written by men, Bob Crew and Kenny Nolan, and Patti LaBelle stated she didn't even know what the song was about. Despite this, the song is significant for empowering the character of "Creole Lady Marmalade," who boldly asks "Voulet Vou Coucher avec moi, c'est soi," presenting a woman in a position of power in a sexual context, marking progress in the portrayal of female sexuality in music. "What Lady Marmalade shows us is that it does not have to be."

This is the original 1970s "delightfully raunchy" soul classic about New Orleans sex workers. The song had already reached number one on the Hot 100 once, way back in 1975. Tom Bryan of Stereo Gum described the song as existing "at some genre-free nether realm where disco and soul and funk and rock all intersect," and noted that the original version was "already pretty perfect." "Lady Marmalade, the delightfully raunchy, La Belle classic about New Orleans sex workers, which we discussed in last year's R&B Queen's episode of Hit Parade, had already gone to number one on the Hot 100 once, way back in 1975."
